page: Microsoft Azure D32ds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 260 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance includes a bundled 1890 GB local disk and supports Premium Storage. No GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance in specific workloads, particularly in text processing, image processing, and single-threaded gzip compression, which all rank in the top 25%. In Passmark CPU testing, the physics test achieved a strong rating, while the overall Passmark CPU score and database operations fell within the average range. Memory performance presents a tradeoff, with a weak Passmark memory score despite average read-only and write large-block memory bandwidths. For language model workloads, the server demonstrates top-tier performance in text generation for small 135M models, alongside strong prompt processing speeds for both small and medium 7B models.

The qualitative cost efficiency of the D32ds_v6 is defined by its high-density local storage and dedicated Intel Xeon compute resources, which offset the lower relative memory performance. This hardware profile is well-suited for general-purpose enterprise workloads, static web serving, software compilation, and database operations that benefit from fast local disk access. It is also capable of handling moderate-scale LLM inference tasks and text or image processing pipelines without requiring dedicated GPU acceleration.
